problem:
The equation below gives a parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(3,2,-1)$ and $Q(0,1,-3).$

$$
r(t)=a\,i+b\,j-(2t+1)\,k,\,t\in [0,c]
$$

What is $a+b+c?$

feedback.problem:
The equation below gives a parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(-4,0,-3)$ and $Q(-6,2,-5).$

$$
r(t)=-a\,i+2t\,j-b\,k,\,t\in [0,c]
$$

What is $a+b+c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(-6\,i+2\,j-5\,k)-(-4\,i-3\,k) \\  & =-2\,i+2\,j-2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=(-4\,i-3\,k)+t(-2\,i+2\,j-2\,k)
$$

and the parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(-4\,i-3\,k)+t(-2\,i+2\,j-2\,k) \\  & =-(2t+4)\,i+2t\,j-(2t+3)\,k,\,t\in [0,1].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=(2t+4)+(2t+3)+1=4t+8.
$$
